Why MediDecode exists. Three things go wrong for almost every patient and family after a doctor visit — this portal is built to fix all three.

PROBLEM 01

Unreadable prescriptions

Handwritten prescriptions are rushed and hard to read. Families guess doses, chemists misread names, and the wrong medicine or wrong timing can follow.

PROBLEM 02

Hidden interaction risks

Two common medicines together — or a medicine with the wrong food — can reduce the effect or harm the liver, stomach or heart. Nobody checks this at home.

PROBLEM 03

Paying 3×–5× extra

A branded strip and its generic contain the exact same salt, yet the brand can cost three to five times more. Most patients never hear the word “generic”.

🛡️

Drug Interaction Checker

Stay safe — every decoded medicine is cross-checked against the others, plus common foods and alcohol.

⚠ High — Duplicate Salt

Dolo 650 + Zerodol-P both contain Paracetamol

Taking both together can push paracetamol above the safe 4,000 mg/day limit and damage the liver. This is the most common home-medication mistake in India.

→ Action: Take only ONE of them at a time. Confirm with your doctor before combining.

◆ Moderate — Stomach Risk

Zerodol-P (Aceclofenac) on an empty stomach

Aceclofenac is an NSAID painkiller. On an empty stomach it can cause acidity, gastritis and, with long use, stomach bleeding — especially in older patients.

→ Action: Always take after food. Pan-D in the morning already protects the stomach — do not skip it.

◆ Food Interaction

Augmentin 625 works best WITH food

Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid absorbs better and causes less nausea when taken at the start of a meal. Pan-D is the opposite — it must be taken 30 minutes BEFORE breakfast.

→ Action: Pan-D first (empty stomach), Augmentin with breakfast and dinner.

◆ Alcohol Warning

No alcohol during this course

Alcohol + paracetamol increases liver strain, and alcohol + antibiotics can cause nausea, flushing and dizziness while slowing recovery from infection.

→ Action: Avoid alcohol until 48 hours after the last antibiotic dose.

🌡 SOS — Only if needed (not a routine dose)

Dolo 650 — 1 tablet, after food, only if fever is above 101°F or pain is severe. Maximum 3 tablets in 24 hours, and never at the same time as Zerodol-P — both contain paracetamol. If fever crosses 103°F or lasts beyond 3 days, see your doctor.

Under the hood — the tech stack. Built as a Python + web system: a FastAPI backend does the heavy lifting, the browser handles tracking and offline access.

FastAPI · Python

API Backend

Receives the prescription image, runs the full decode pipeline and returns structured medicine data as JSON in seconds.

OpenCV + PaddleOCR

Image + Handwriting OCR

OpenCV deskews, sharpens and denoises the photo; PaddleOCR reads the handwriting, doses and frequency codes like BD / TID.

RapidFuzz

Fuzzy Medicine Matching

OCR text is never perfect — RapidFuzz fuzzy-matches it against a drug database (“Augmentn” → Augmentin 625) with a confidence score.

NetworkX

Interaction Graph

Drugs, salts and foods are nodes in a graph; edges carry known interactions. Every new prescription is checked against the whole graph.

ReportLab

Printable Schedule

Generates the clean A4 daily dosage timetable as a PDF that families can print and stick on the fridge.

HTML · CSS · JS + Service Worker

Frontend + Offline Access

Interactive dosage timeline and savings calculator in the browser; a Service Worker caches the timetable so it opens even with no internet in an emergency.

📷 Photo→OpenCV Clean→PaddleOCR→RapidFuzz Match→NetworkX Check→Generic Lookup→📋 Timetable

About MediDecode

Smarter healthcare, a healthier you.

MediDecode is built to make medicine simple — helping you decode prescriptions, find affordable alternatives and stay informed about your health, with the power of technology. Upload a photo and it extracts medicine names, dosages and schedules, flags interaction warnings, suggests verified generic salt equivalents with price comparisons, and exports a clean daily dosage timetable.

Built with 💜 for better healthcare — an educational project demo for classroom presentation.

🚨 In an emergency

If someone has taken a wrong or double dose and has vomiting, severe dizziness, breathing trouble or unusual sleepiness — do not wait. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital, and carry this decoded medicine list with you.

Call 112
Medical disclaimer: MediDecode is an educational project demo. It helps you understand a prescription — it does not replace your doctor or pharmacist. Always confirm any warning, substitution or dose change with a qualified medical professional before acting on it. Prices shown are representative demo prices for common Indian brands and generics; actual prices vary by store and city. Uploaded images are sent to Google Gemini for detection and reading, and prices in a live decode are AI estimates — confirm both with your pharmacist.
